subject: SIG-Lite: chain-of-deps evidence and tertiary dependency attestation
messages:
From: Alice Meyer <alice.meyer@healthsilo.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Security Team <security@healthsilo.com>
Date: Fri, 18 Dec 2026 09:14:00 -0800
Subject: Request: SIG-Lite chain-of-deps and tertiary dependency attestations

Hi Jonas,

Thanks for taking this on — HealthSilo's procurement and security teams are running a SIG-Lite review for our Proof-of-Concept. Two asks we need to close by Dec 24:

1) A flat inventory of all subprocessors you rely on for the inference path (model hosting, embeddings, telemetry, logging, KMS, S3) with vendor name, country, and whether they process customer content.
2) A mapping that shows "depth" (first-party, second-party, tertiary) for downstream dependencies and any reasonable attestations for encryption, KMS tenancy, and EU data processing.

We don't need full SOC 2 evidence yet, but SIG-Lite consumable artifacts (spreadsheet + a short zip with supporting attestations) would be ideal. Also flag any vendors that are single points of failure or that hold raw customer prompts.

Can you confirm owners and an ETA? We can extend to Dec 28 if needed but would like an intermediate status by Monday.

Appreciate it —
Alice
Alice Meyer
Head of Vendor Assurance, HealthSilo

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Alice Meyer <alice.meyer@healthsilo.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 18 Dec 2026 11:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: SIG-Lite chain-of-deps and tertiary dependency attestations

Hi Alice —

Thanks for the clear asks. Marissa will lead the inventory and SCA depth mapping; Sean will validate the KMS/encryption notes and confirm where customer prompts may be persisted for telemetry. I'll own the submission and point of contact for follow-ups.

Quick plan:
- Monday (Dec 21) — deliver initial spreadsheet (flattened registry) and a short diagram explaining the inference request flow.
- Tuesday (Dec 22) — follow-up zip with supporting attestations (vendor statements, links to SOC/SIG where available) and SCA depth spreadsheet.

Items we'll flag up front: Redwood uses a combination of managed object storage (multi-region), our hosted model catalog (open models we serve on infra), a telemetry pipeline with sampling that stores hashed request metadata, and a KMS provider for key wrapping. We'll identify exactly which third parties carry customer prompts.

If HealthSilo would like us to exclude any non-essential metadata fields from the export, call that out now.

Jonas Weber
Director, Trust & Security (Redwood Inference)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Alice Meyer <alice.meyer@healthsilo.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 19 Dec 2026 10:35:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: SIG-Lite chain-of-deps and tertiary dependency attestations

Hi Alice / team —

Attached is our initial delivery per the plan:
- redwood_subprocessor_registry_v2.csv (flat list: role, vendor, country, processes_customer_content [yes/no], contact, retention boundary)
- sca-depth-mapping-2026.xlsx (tabs: inference-path, dataflows, tertiary-mapping)
- thirdparty-dataflow-diagram.png (high-level flow showing where data crosses vendor boundaries)
- sig-lite-evidence-2026.zip (contains vendor attestation PDFs and links to public compliance pages)

Summary notes:
- First-party: Redwood runtime + our autoscaling pool. We are primary processor and control the runtime kernel.
- Second-party: Managed object storage (RedCloud Storage) and KMS (KeySphere) — both engaged for persistence and key management; KeySphere is configured in dedicated tenancy for enterprise customers where requested.
- Tertiary: Small set of monitoring vendors used for agentless metrics and aggregated telemetry; none receive unmasked prompts by default. We do retain sampled request metadata for anomaly detection; raw prompts are only written to storage in two circumstances (a) explicit debug session where customer enables logging, (b) billing/abuse investigations subject to retention policy. Both circumstances are called out in the registry column 'stores_raw_prompts'.

Open items we will follow up on Monday:
- A brief vendor statement from KeySphere about tenant isolation (we have it on request but need to extract the short quote).
- Confirmation of the retention TTL on sampled telemetry (currently 90 days, will validate).

Attachments referenced above are included in this thread. Let me know if you want a CSV filtered for EU-only vendors first.

-Marissa
Marissa Cole
Senior Security Programs Manager, Redwood Inference

From: Alice Meyer <alice.meyer@healthsilo.com>

Marissa —

Thanks for the fast turnaround, this is helpful. Two clarifying items before we mark this complete:

1) KeySphere tenancy: can you provide a one-paragraph attestation on whether enterprise keys are in a logical multi-tenant HSM or in a physically isolated tenant for HealthSilo? A short, signed PDF would do.
2) EU processing: please provide a filtered registry view showing any subprocessors that could process EU resident data and whether data-in-transit crosses regions (yes/no).

If you can add those in the zip and drop a single-spotlight PDF with the KMS paragraph, we can close the SIG-Lite. Do not include vendor confidential attachments unless they are vendor-signed statements.

Thanks —
Alice
